Chapter 6
Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales
QM integration with SAP S/4HANA Sales brings far greater visibility to
the logistics, operations, and supply chain management processes.
Integrating QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales helps organizations ensure that only accept-
able and approved products eventually reach the customer. Organizations may also
have requirements that the customer inspect the product before or after a product’s
delivery.
This chapter begins by covering the configuration basics of setting up QM with SAP
S/4HANA Sales. Then, the focus shifts to required QM master data before culminating
in running the entire end-to-end business process of various sales cycles. Because
you’ve seen master data creation processes extensively in Chapter 2, here we provide
the SAP S/4HANA Sales and QM master data checklist just for you to make sure that
it’s available in the system.
Table 6.1 consists of various inspection types that find greater usage in sales processes
and into which you can integrate the QM area.
6.1 Configuration Basics
The following are the configuration settings that you need to ensure are available:
 Assignment of inspection lot origin to delivery type
 Assignment of inspection type to delivery category

To assign an inspection lot origin to a relevant delivery type, follow menu path SAP
IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot Creation  Inspection at
Shipping  Assign Inspection Lot Origin to Delivery Type (see Figure 6.1 1).
Figure 6.1 Inspection Type and Inspection Origin Assignments
First, you assign the inspection lot origin to the relevant delivery type. You already know
that you can’t change the inspection lot origin; therefore, logically assigning the inspec-
tion lot origin to delivery types ensures that the necessary business functions work cor-
rectly. For example, inspection origin 06 is specific to customer returns, so assigning
this inspection origin for all delivery types for customer returns makes sense.
In this example, assign inspection lot origin 10 to delivery type (DlvTy) LF (Outbound
Delivery), 11 to LO (Delivery w/o Ref.), and 06 to LR (Returns Delivery). Although it isn’t
shown, also assign inspection lot origin 12 to delivery type LO2 (Delivery w/o Ref.) in
Figure 6.1 1. We’ll show the associated business process later in this chapter. Inspection
origin 12 is for inspection for general delivery.
The second configuration step is to assign the inspection type to a delivery category.
Follow menu path SAP IMG  Quality Management  Quality Inspection  Inspection Lot
Creation  Inspection at Shipping  Assign Inspection Type to Delivery Category 2. Here,
you can assign inspection types of relevant inspection origin to the relevant delivery
category (Delv.Cat). If you’ve configured a specific inspection type to cater to a business
need, then you can assign it in this step. The different usage of a delivery category is
shown in Figure 6.1 2.
6.2 Master Data
Ensure that the following SAP S/4HANA Sales master data is available in the SAP S/4HANA
system:
© 

311
6.2 Master Data
 Material master, including complete maintenance of sales views
 Business partner in a customer role
 Material pricing condition
The QM master data that you need is as follows:
 Inspection types 06, 10, 11, and 12 active in the QM view of the material master of the
finished good
 Inspection plan usage 6 (goods issue) having status 4 (for released) for all four
inspection types
 Quality information record: SD
A quality information record (SD) is a relationship between materials that the cus-
tomer orders. In this specific master data creation step, you maintain the QM integra-
tion relationship with SAP S/4HANA Sales.
To create a quality information record (SD), use Transaction QV51 or follow menu path
Logistics  Quality Management  Quality Planning  Logistics Master Data  Quality Info
Record: SD  Create. On the initial screen that appears, enter Customer “17100003” and
Sales Organization “1710”, and choose Control Data. The screen in Figure 6.2 appears;
choose Edit  New Info Record (not shown; located on bottom-right side of the screen)
to go to the dialog for creating new data, and proceed as follows:
1. Enter the Material as “QM001”.
2. Choose the Delivery cat.. If there is no specific category, leave it blank.
3. Enter a short text for Additional information (optional).
4. Choose the Before delivery radio button in the Quality inspection area. Here, if you
choose Before delivery, then the system requires you to perform QM functions
before you can issue goods. For After delivery, the system allows goods issuance, and
you can subsequently perform QM functions. The By customer option refers to spe-
cial cases when the customer inspects the goods to confirm that they meet the spec-
ifications.
5. Save the customer information record.
Figure 6.2 also shows one important difference: customer information records control
individual materials for a customer, whereas customer specifications apply to all mate-
rials of a customer. This example is based on a customer information record, which
provides better differentiation in terms of material assignment.
Tips and Tricks
When choosing Documents in Figure 6.2, you also have the option to link the quality
information record with a quality document (e.g., quality assurance agreements or
special specifications). In the dialog window for linking the QM information record to
documents, use the input help to choose the document that you want to attach.

6.3 Business Processes
This section covers the following four business processes in SAP S/4HANA Sales:
 Customer delivery with sales order
 Customer delivery without sales order
 Return order
 General delivery
6.3.1 Customer Delivery with Sales Order
The customer places an order for a material, for which you create a sales order. When
you’re ready to deliver the material with reference to the sales order, you first create an
outbound delivery. At this time, the system informs you in the status bar that the qual-
ity inspection is being prepared. You perform the QM functions, such as results record-
ing and usage decision. Next, you post goods issue with reference to the outbound
delivery and proceed to bill the customer and receive payment (not covered in this
chapter). Figure 6.3 depicts this business process.

At the item level, enter Material “QM001” and the Order Quantity “10” PC. There is sig-
nificantly more information that you can maintain in the sales order, but this is the
minimum information that you need to maintain. If you navigate to the item’s details
view of the material, you can also maintain its usage that the system will refer to while
creating the inspection lot of the relevant inspection type.
Notice that the Requested Deliv.Date (required delivery date) in this case is 02/24/
2024. Save the sales order, and the system creates sales order number 5612 in this
example.
Using Transaction VL01N, the initial screen will the Outbound Delivery with Order Ref-
erence screen. Here, enter Shipping Point “1710”, Selection Date “02/24/2024” (the
delivery date covered in the previous step), and (sales) Order “5612”. Because the config-
uration of the sales order automatically picks up the relevant delivery type, you don’t
need to enter anything in this field. This leads to Figure 6.5.
Figure 6.5 Outbound Delivery with Reference to Sales Order
In the screen in Figure 6.5, select the line item for which you want to create an out-
bound delivery. Further, at this stage, you also need to enter the pick quantity as 10 PC,
which in this example is the same as the order quantity. A pick quantity is the actual
quantity that you pick or load to create delivery. If you try to issue goods for the out-
bound delivery at this time by choosing Post Goods Issue, you’ll see an error message
at the bottom of the screen (not shown).
The system creates inspection lot 100000000308 while you’re still creating the out-
bound delivery for the sales order. Because you set the Before delivery radio button in
the quality information record (SD) for the customer/material/plant combination, you
must first perform quality functions before the system allows you to post goods issue

In due course, you record results and undertake usage decision for inspection lot

6.3.2 Customer Delivery without Sales Order
You can create inspection lots for a customer delivery for which there is no sales order
(or customer order) reference. This may be the case when the customer requests urgent

6 Integrating with SAP S/4HANA Sales

or immediate delivery without first issuing an order (a purchase order for the customer
and sales order for the company).
Access the screen in Figure 6.7 using Transaction VL01NO, and enter Shipping Point
“1710” and Delivery Type “LO”, as well as the details of the organizational data, such as
Sales Organization “1710”, Distribution Channel “10”, and Division “00”, and press
(Enter).
In Figure 6.8, enter the customer, who is also ship-to party “17100003” in this case. At
the item level, enter Material “QM001” and the Order Quantity of “10” PC; select the
line item for which you want to create the outbound delivery. At this stage, you also
need to enter the Picked Quantity of “10” PC. Here, again, if you try to issue goods for
the outbound delivery at this time by choosing Post Goods Issue, an error message
appears, explaining that the system created inspection lot 110000000000 when you
were still creating the delivery without reference to a sales order. Because you set the
Before delivery radio button in the quality information record (SD) for the customer/
material/plant combination, you must perform quality functions before the system
allows you to post goods issue for the delivery. Save the outbound delivery, and the sys-
tem creates delivery number 80005138.
Figure 6.7 Customer Delivery without Sales Order Reference
Meanwhile, after performing all the necessary quality functions, the system creates
inspection lot 110000000000. The system now allows you to post goods issue by
using Transaction VL02N and by entering delivery number 80005138.
Figure 6.9 shows the Inspection Lot 110000000000 of Inspection Type 11 (Transaction
QA03), for which the system creates customer delivery without reference to sales
order. The reference of Delivery 80005138 is available in the inspection lot.

6.3.3 Return Order
A return order may occur due to defective or damaged goods or excess or slow-moving
products that the customer returns and the company accepts. Figure 6.10 shows the
steps involved in the business process of a return order:
1. Create the return order (order type RE; Transaction VA01).
2. Create the outbound delivery with reference to a return order (Transaction VL01N).
3. Perform QM functions such as results recording and usage decision. There is no
stock posting involved.
4. Post goods receipt (Transaction VL02N). Because this is a customer return and is
with reference to the return order, the system automatically provides the option to
post goods receipt using this transaction.
5. Issue the credit memo.
Figure 6.10 Business Process Flow for Return Orders
Figure 6.11 shows Inspection Lot 60000000000 of Inspection Type 06 (Transaction
QA03), which the system creates for Sales Order (return order) 60000235. The reference
of Delivery 84000105 is also available in the inspection lot that the system created for
this delivery type.
Tips and Tricks
If the customer returns defective or damaged goods to the company, the company
must inspect them before receiving them into its stock. In this business scenario, you
can integrate inspection type 05 (other goods receipt). Refer to Chapter 4, Section 4.5.2,
which covers inspection type 05, for more information.

6.3.4 General Delivery
The steps involved in the business process of general delivery are as follows:
1. Create a delivery without reference (Transaction VL01NO). On the initial screen, in
the Delivery Type field, enter “LO2”. Remember that you’ve already ensured that the
necessary configuration settings of inspection origin 12 for delivery type LO2 are in
place (refer to Figure 6.1).
2. Perform QM functions such as results recording and usage decision.
3. Post goods issue (Transaction VL02N).

QA03), which the system creates for general delivery. At this time, it contains reference
to only customer 17100003, but after you record results, make a usage decision, and

Note

6.4 Summary
6.4 Summary
Standard solutions and configurations delivered by SAP S/4HANA are sufficient to
independently configure, implement, and integrate QM into SAP S/4HANA Sales busi-
ness processes. By making necessary configuration settings and then setting up the rel-
evant QM master data, a one-time task, you can quickly and comprehensively integrate
QM with SAP S/4HANA Sales. You can also leverage quality certificate functionality to
issue outgoing quality certificates for goods that you send to customers.
The next chapter covers integrating QM with plant maintenance (PM), specifically for
test equipment management.
